evidence: Cic. Att. 6.1.13: holusculīs nōs solēs pāscere
terms.comment: First of animals, which it also takes out to graze; of people too, as when Cicero teases Atticus for always feeding him vegetables. The passive pāscor is to feed, to graze.
Rare. Suetonius’s Tiberius fed his pet snake by hand; with people as object the verb is late (Vulgate).

evidence: Tac. Germ. 20.1: sua quemque māter ūberibus alit
terms.comment: Feeding that brings up: a mother nursing her baby.

phrases.latin: vēlōcēs Spartae catulōs ācremque Molossum pāsce serō pinguī
phrases.english: feed the swift Spartan puppies and the fierce mastiff on rich whey

phrases.latin: Respicite volātilia caelī … et Pater vester caelestis pāscit illa.
phrases.english: Look at the birds of the air … and your heavenly Father feeds them.
